subject: Astronomy & Space
title: How the Moon Formed
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on How the Moon Formed.

hook.text: About 4.5 billion years ago, a Mars-sized body slammed into early Earth. The debris became our Moon.

buildup.text: The giant impact hypothesis is the leading theory. The collision vaporized rock, which collected in orbit and cooled.

discovery.text: Apollo samples showed the Moon's composition closely matches Earth's mantle—strong evidence for the impact theory.

twist.text: The impactor, called Theia, may have been absorbed into Earth. Blobs of its material might still exist deep in the mantle.

climax.text: Without the Moon, Earth's axial tilt would wobble wildly. Our Moon stabilizes seasons and may have helped life evolve.

punchline.text: Born from a world-shattering collision. The Moon may be why life thrived here.

quiz.question: What is the leading theory for how Earth's Moon formed?
options: A Mars-sized body collided with early Earth, and debris formed the Moon
The Moon was captured by Earth's gravity as it passed by
The Moon split off from a rapidly spinning young Earth

details.summary: The leading theory for the Moon's origin is the Giant Impact Hypothesis: about 4.5 billion years ago, a Mars-sized body called Theia collided with the young Earth, blasting debris into orbit that coalesced to form the Moon.
details.whyItMatters: The Moon's formation shaped Earth's early history — stabilizing its axial tilt, slowing its rotation, and driving tides that may have been crucial for life's origin. Understanding this violent birth illuminates planetary formation broadly.
takeaways: A Mars-sized body likely collided with early Earth
Debris from the impact coalesced into the Moon
This explains the Moon's composition and orbital properties

faq.question: What evidence supports the Giant Impact Hypothesis?
faq.answer: Apollo lunar samples show the Moon's isotopic composition is nearly identical to Earth's mantle — consistent with forming from Earth's material. The Moon has a small iron core relative to its size (the impact stripped mainly mantle material).

faq.question: Are there alternative theories for the Moon's origin?
faq.answer: Historically, three alternatives were proposed: co-accretion (forming together), fission (spinning off from Earth), and capture (gravitationally caught). None explain the geochemical and dynamical evidence as well as the giant impact.
